pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
When the number of args to the logger was incorrect, we would raise instead of saving the log message
which made it difficult to figure out what went wrong. Additionally, this was easy to miss in the code since
the problem can't happen when running under pytest since it overrides the logging handlers.

fixes #80642
fixes #63600
will make it easier to track down #74584

I added a bit of typing here since I hard such a hard time tracing down this issue.

issue_context.title: Improve Error Logging when issue with message format
issue_context.body:
### The problem

A formatting issue was reported, but as this is related to a message from a thread and given the limited information it's not straightforward to find the source.
I have not been able to replicate it but that should be possible when knowing how the thread log messages work.

The issue is that "TypeError: not enough arguments for format string" is not enough to determine what caused it.

```raw
2022-01-07 15:04:58 ERROR (Thread-2) [root] Uncaught thread exception
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.9/threading.py", line 973, in _bootstrap_inner
    self.run()
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.9/threading.py", line 910, in run
    self._target(*self._args, **self._kwargs)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.9/logging/handlers.py", line 1518, in _monitor
    self.handle(record)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.9/logging/handlers.py", line 1499, in handle
    handler.handle(record)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.9/logging/__init__.py", line 952, in handle
    self.emit(record)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/system_log/__init__.py", line 191, in emit
    entry = LogEntry(record, stack, _figure_out_source(record, stack, self.hass))
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/system_log/__init__.py", line 98, in __init
    self.message = deque([record.getMessage()], maxlen=5)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.9/logging/__init__.py", line 367, in getMessage
    msg = msg % self.args
TypeError: not enough arguments for format string
`` 

I suggest that this exception is captured in the thread and that the unformatted message would be logged instead - with or without all arguments converted to strings (as they would have to be for the message).

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2021.12.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

Home Assistant OS

Trying to find cause for last 4-5 months.
Did not find anything. A lot of hours spent to find cause and nothing. Reinstallation of raspbian, reinstallation of HA, reinstallation of integrations , changing SDD and .... nothing.

review_comments: Where is the assertion? What's different with the critical logger compared to the warning logger?

Critical and warning will both do the same, but there must be at least one valid argument, and at least one missing argument to trigger the exception in logging since the base logging module has a guard to check for `self.args`:

https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/ba6492e2a705ebbe140fdf8734114156e55b3c9a/Lib/logging/__init__.py#L367

This will hit this exception trap when not run under pytest (which patches logging)
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/80645/files#diff-d7d18627b016b0d21ad36d10f06b43146746bf30e77d78ecf7851c579f6795f1R101
Is the test not testing the code then?

Its not hitting that line as its not possible to do so under pytest since the logging is trapped. 

Any thoughts on a way to make this testable within the test suite or is this a case where we have to settle for manual testing ?
To disable the pytest capture or logging plugin we'd need a separate CI job, it seems. We could add that and just run the logger tests, if we think it's important.

I think the added maintenance burden doesn't justify the cost of adding another CI job.

Additionally I think the risk of someone modifying this and causing a regression is low.

I'm going to add some additional comments and details in the doc strings to mitigate that risk.
Sounds good.
I still think we should remove this test, since it doesn't seem to do anything.
